what: SIMULATED traffic-analysis defences at the feature level (not a measurement on a real gateway)

attackers.non_adaptive: classifier trained on clean traffic of other configs, shown defended traffic of unseen configs
attackers.adaptive: classifier retrained on defended traffic of other configs (knows the defence), tested on unseen configs

pad_buckets.label: Pad packets to size buckets
pad_buckets.description: every packet padded up to the next of (128, 256, 512, 1024, 1500) bytes

pad_mtu.label: Pad every packet to full size

dummy.label: Constant-rate dummy traffic
dummy.description: 40 dummy packets per second of 600 bytes

shape.label: Timing shaping
shape.description: packets held until the next 100 ms slot

combined.label: Combined
combined.description: size buckets + dummy traffic + random delay

caveats: Feature-level simulation on scripted lab traffic: real padding/dummy-traffic implementations differ in detail.
The adaptive attacker uses the same 12 window features; a stronger attacker (sequence models, longer windows) may do better.
Captures are short (file transfer, VoIP and video < 2 s), which limits how well dummy traffic and shaping can be judged.
Costs are per capture and depend on how busy the capture is: padding a ping stream costs a lot, padding a bulk transfer almost nothing.
